evals.name: HTTP Controller Decoupling & 202 Accepted Response
evals.prompt: Refactor a synchronous invoice export endpoint that generates large PDFs and sends emails within the HTTP controller to enqueue a job to BullMQ/SQS and return an immediate HTTP 202 Accepted response.
evals.expected_output: Enqueues job to background message queue and responds immediately with 202 Accepted, jobId, and poll URL.
assertions: Removes heavy PDF generation and email sending operations from the HTTP controller
Enqueues job to message queue with versioned payload and unique tracking identifier
Returns HTTP 202 Accepted status immediately to prevent client request timeouts
Provides job tracking identifier or status poll URL in response payload

evals.name: Exponential Backoff Retries with Jitter & DLQ Routing
evals.prompt: Configure a background job consumer with exponential backoff and randomized jitter for transient failure retries, and route to a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) when maximum retry attempts are exhausted.
evals.expected_output: Calculates exponential delay with jitter for retries and sends exhausted jobs to DLQ with error context.
assertions: Calculates exponential delay across consecutive retry attempts
Applies randomized jitter (e.g. 10-20% or full jitter) to prevent thundering herds
Transfers permanently failed jobs to a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) after max attempts
Attaches terminal failure diagnostic details and stack traces to DLQ payload

evals.name: Consumer Idempotency Safeguards & Deduplication Table
evals.prompt: Implement an idempotent payment processing worker that prevents duplicate charges if the message queue delivers the same job message multiple times.
evals.expected_output: Verifies idempotency key in deduplication store before execution and commits transaction atomically.
assertions: Checks unique idempotencyKey before executing irreversible business operations
Skips duplicate job execution safely if key has already been marked as processed
Records processed key atomically within business transaction or deduplication table
Guarantees at-least-once queue delivery does not cause duplicate side effects
